# Model Context Protocol (MCP)

Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a rulebook that tells an AI agent how to pack background information before it sends a prompt to a language model. It lists what pieces go into the promptΓÇöthings like the system role, the userΓÇÖs request, past memory, tool calls, or code snippetsΓÇöand fixes their order. Clear tags mark each piece, so both humans and machines can see where one part ends and the next begins. Keeping the format steady cuts confusion, lets different tools work together, and makes it easier to test or swap models later. When agents follow MCP, the model gets a clean, complete prompt and can give better answers.
